answer: A garden admits an operator's kth identity only when its sonnet, chained to the previous sonnet's hash, carries k leading zero bits. Mining that sonnet burns an expected \(2^k\) basalt, so the tenth burns 1024 and ten together 2046; a first burns two. Each sonnet must include the prior hash, so the work cannot be split across parallel identities. The garden writes the chain to the operator's signed root, and a successor garden reopens it, so a fresh root cannot carry the operator's existing identities.
